Subject: Hosted API latency commitments — measurement + penalty questions

Jordan —

Thanks for the demo last week. Brightline is sizing the integration and our procurement team has asked for concrete latency commitments for the hosted API (we need p50/p95 targets and how you measure them). A few specific asks: 

- What are typical p50 / p95 numbers we should expect for chat generation at 512 tokens for the curated models?
- How do you define the measurement window for SLOs (rolling day, 7 day, monthly?) and do you sample or weight by region?
- If an SLO is missed, what is your penalty / credit approach? Any staged / graduated approach?
- Are there carveouts for planned maintenance, regional cloud outages, or bursts caused by customer traffic?

We're trying to avoid one-size-fits-all language in the contract. Would appreciate a short proposal so we can include it in our security & procurement review.

Timothy Chase
Head of Platform Integrations
Brightline Inc.

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Timothy Chase <timothy@brightline.com>
Date: Sun, 16 May 2027 12:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Hosted API latency commitments — measurement + penalty questions

Hi Timothy —

Appreciate the clear list — below is a concise proposal we think balances reliability with predictable economics. This is intended as a starting point you can drop into procurement. Happy to iterate.

Proposal (hosted API, curated models, gen-512):
- Performance commitments (measured at request-response completion):
  - p50 <= 120 ms
  - p95 <= 450 ms
- Measurement method: rolling 30-day window, measured at 1-minute sampling granularity and aggregated across regions by traffic-weighted averaging. We trim the top 0.5% of outliers per-day to avoid skew from noisy probes.
- Carveouts: planned maintenance windows (48-hour advance notice) and verified cloud provider incidents are excluded. Short-lived regional bursts that are <5 minutes per incident are excluded up to 3 incidents/month.
- Penalty / remediation: graduated service credit tiers rather than an immediate invoice-level penalty — credits applied to that month's invoice:
  - If p95 misses by <= 10% of target: 5% service credit
  - If p95 misses by >10% and <= 30%: 15% service credit + priority mitigation plan
  - If p95 misses by >30%: 25% service credit + executive review and dedicated remediation resources
- Fallbacks: we offer an automatic fallback to a higher-capacity model variant within the same catalog (no data access change) to preserve availability; this can be opt-in for Brightline.

Notes: The values above assume normal production traffic and our recommended configuration (prefix caching enabled, standard batching). If you expect heavy short-lived spikes (e.g., large marketing events), we should discuss burst capacity reserves to avoid credit exposure.

If that looks reasonable I can loop in our pricing/procurement team for final language and add the SLO draft as an exhibit to the MSA.

Best,

Jordan —

Good summary. A few product/ops/legal touches below — keeping the spirit of your proposal but tightening some thresholds and clarifying measurement semantics so that we don't open a large false-positive window for credits.

Suggested edits (redlines for the exhibit):
- Measurement window: recommend a 30-day rolling window (keep) but use a two-phase aggregation: per-region 30-day p95, then traffic-weighted aggregation across regions. This prevents a noisy low-traffic region from triggering credits.
- Outlier trim: increase trim from 0.5% to 1.0% daily for probe-level noise mitigation; document that synthetic probes are excluded from SLO calculations (we only use customer traffic).
- Regional burst carveout: restate as 'regional incident carveout if an incident impacts >20% of region capacity for >10 minutes' — keeps it measurable. Keep the small-incident exclusion for <5 minutes but cap to 2 incidents/month (we can't have unlimited carveouts).
- Credits ladder: keep graduated credits but cap total credits to 25% of the monthly invoice. Also include a 'remediation credit' (non-monetary) — waived onboarding fees for next quarter if two consecutive months miss the SLO.
- Planned maintenance: require at least 72 hours notice for any maintenance that will exceed 30 minutes of region impact.

Implementation/ops notes:
- We'll publish a per-model performance profile in the Console as an appendix — that will set realistic expectations for p50/p95 at given token lengths and config knobs (batching, kv cache).
- For pricing: Karthik, suggest a 4% SR uplift for accounts that require a strict 30-day rolling SLO with the fallback opt-in disabled (i.e., they want strict guarantees without our automatic mitigation). If Brightline chooses the fallback-to-higher-capacity-model option, we'll keep standard pricing but require a 2-week capacity warmup window.

I attached a marked-up SLO exhibit (slo-draft-20270516.pdf) and a short example spreadsheet showing per-region aggregation (measurement-examples-rows.xlsx).

If Jordan can confirm Brightline is comfortable with staged credits capped at 25% and the regional thresholds above, I can send a final redline to procurement/legal.
